import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 208
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/208](https://www.erdosproblems.com/208)
-/

open Filter Real

namespace Erdos208

/-- The sequence of squarefree numbers, denoted by `s` as in Erdős problem 208. -/
noncomputable def erdos208.s : ℕ → ℕ := Nat.nth Squarefree

open erdos208

/--
Let $s_1 < s_2 < \dots$ be the sequence of squarefree numbers. Is it true that
for any $\epsilon > 0$ and large $n$, $s_{n+1} - s_n \ll_\epsilon s_n^\epsilon$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_208.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), (fun n => (s (n + 1) - s n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n => (s n : ℝ)^ε) := by sorry

/--
Let $s_1 < s_2 < \dots$ be the sequence of squarefree numbers. Is it true that
$s_{n + 1} - s_n \le (1 + o(1)) \cdot (\pi^2 / 6) \cdot \log (s_n) / \log (\log (s_n))$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_208.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (c : ℕ → ℝ), (c =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      s (n + 1) - s n ≤ (1 + (c n)) * (π^2 / 6) * log (s n) / log (log (s n)) := by
  sorry

/--
In [Er79] Erdős says perhaps $s_{n+1} - s_n \ll \log s_n$, but he is 'very doubtful'.

[Er79] Erdős, Paul, __Some unconventional problems in number theory__. Math. Mag. (1979), 67-70.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_208.variants.log_bound :
    (fun n ↦ (s (n + 1) - s n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ log (s n) := by sorry

end Erdos208

reformulations.difference: The source’s multiplicative error `1 + o(1)` is represented by an existential real sequence `c`, with `c =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)`, followed by an eventual inequality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The function `(1 : ℕ → ℝ)` is constantly one. Mathlib’s little-o condition is equivalent to `Tendsto c atTop (𝓝 0)`, and eventuality on ℕ is equivalent to holding for every n beyond some cutoff. The full equivalence with this explicit limit-and-cutoff formulation was proved in the scratch file. Also, s tends to infinity, so log(log(s n)) is eventually positive; its small-input values do not change the claim.

reformulations.difference: The original 1979 paper writes the tentative bound using `log n`; Lean follows the problem website in using `log(s n)`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Squarefree integers have natural density 6/π², so their increasing enumeration satisfies s_n ∼ (π²/6)n. Consequently log(s_n)/log n tends to one, making the two big-O bounds equivalent. Zero-based indexing and replacing a strict bound by a non-strict big-O bound do not affect this asymptotic assertion.

sources_consulted: T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problem #208, read in the 3 September 2026 snapshot: https://web.archive.org/web/20260903202752id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/208
P. Erdős, Some unconventional problems in number theory, Mathematics Magazine 52 (1979), 67–70, especially §6 on p. 69: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-22.pdf
External Erdős Problems database, entry 208, status fields: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/data/problems.yaml
review.notes: Checked the definition and all three theorem statements against the source. No mathematical defects or status discrepancies found. The latest accessible source snapshot still records the problem as open, as does the external status database. Direct access to the live problem page was blocked by Cloudflare, so archived source pages were used. Lean experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully: they verify s(0)=1, s(1)=2, s(2)=3, s(3)=5; strict monotonicity, positivity and unboundedness of s; real subtraction in all three gap expressions; and equivalence of the asymptotic statements with their explicit bound/limit formulations. The zero-based enumeration and exceptional small logarithm inputs are harmless because all bounds concern sufficiently large indices.
